external_narratives.summary: The Bomber Gateway Trust created 'On Freedom's Wings', a full-scale steel-frame representation of an Avro Lancaster Mk1 bomber measuring 26 metres in length with a 31-metre wingspan. The sculpture commemorates Lancaster R5689 VN-N, described as the most photographed Lancaster of the war, which crashed on 18 September 1942 returning from a Baltic Sea mission with the loss of five crew.

narrative: Lancaster R5689 (VN-N) was lost on 18 September 1942, one of the countless aircraft that failed to return during Bomber Command's sustained campaign over occupied Europe. Five crew members were killed. No survivors are recorded. The aircraft is commemorated by a full-sized steel replica Lancaster, titled *On Freedom's Wings*, installed at the Bomber County Gateway near Lincoln — a county that served as the operational heartland of Bomber Command throughout the war. The memorial stands as a permanent tribute to the crews of R5689 and the wider force whose sacrifice went formally unrecognised for decades.
